speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with frequent epistaxis, mucous membrane bleeding, and petechiae. To help me understand the severity and underlying cause of your bleeding disorder, how old are you, and are you currently taking any medications like aspirin or ibuprofen?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

Given your age of 4 and the presentation of isolated mucocutaneous bleeding (epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae) without mention of deep tissue hemorrhage or liver/spleen issues, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of Immune Thrombocytopenia. I would like to confirm this by requesting a complete blood count with platelet count. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_platelets.
